what: Two driven wheels share one chassis. Their speed difference changes the path. Differential steering: vary the wheel speeds to change the turning radius.
try: Reset, load the example program and run it. Watch the path rather than only the encoder values.
Stop the program. Use equal motor settings, then make one wheel slower.
Reset and reverse both wheels. Predict the curve before moving.
why: Each wheel covers its own distance. Equal wheel speeds produce translation; a difference rotates the chassis. Opposite speeds can turn it nearly on the spot.
matters: The same geometry steers mobile robots and tracked vehicles.
question: What happens when one wheel travels farther than the other?
answer: The chassis curves toward the slower wheel. Equal magnitudes in opposite directions largely cancel translation.
further: Compare a broad curve with a tight turn.
Try the pivot-steered rover: its front wheels steer mechanically.
formula: v = (vR + vL) / 2;  yaw rate = (vR − vL) / track width
